The most significant are the utility subsidiary's Y-1 operating cash flow being reported as both $468 million and $515 million, and a quarterly table where the fourth-quarter net income arithmetic does not work. Schedule II also contains an apparent prior-year typo/restatement from $7 million to $70 million that breaks the allowance roll-forward. These issues appear more like presentation/control errors than a pervasive failure of the core statements, but they affect audited financial-statement schedules and cash-flow presentation."}
